chunks: From him, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Sufyan al-Jariri, from Abi Sadiq, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Our state/government is the last of the states, and no House will remain having a state/government except that it ruled before us, so that they would not say when they see our conduct: If we had ruled, we would have conducted ourselves like these people.
And it is the word of Allah, the Exalted: '...and the end is for those who guard (against evil).'
ai.seo_question: Why did previous dynasties rule before the Imams according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (a.s.) elucidates that the Mahdi’s reign will be the ultimate and final dynasty, designed to preemptively silence skeptics who claim that the Ahl al-Bayt’s justice was merely theoretical. By ruling before the final era, previous dynasties served as a foil to demonstrate that the Imams' character was consistent regardless of power, thereby validating the Quranic promise that the final victory belongs to the God-conscious.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: H 493 - It is narrated from Fadhl from Ali bin Hakam from Sufyan Jurairi from Abi Sadiq from Imam Muhammad Baqir (a.s) that he said: “

Our state is the last of the states, no House will remain, except that it would rule before us, so that no one gets an opportunity to say when they observe our acts: If we had ruled, we would have also acted in the same way.
It is the word of Allah, the Exalted: “…and the end is for those who guard (against evil).” [7:128]
